title: Sustaining obesity treatment in routine practice
subtitle: Advisory board pre-read — evidence gaps and HCP education priorities
title_note: Advice sought — not endorsement. No invitations issued. ADIPOSYN is a fictional workshop product; real-trial evidence is cited by PMID/NCT and kept separate from SYN sources.

slides.title: The decision we cannot make alone
bullets: **What evidence should we generate, and what should we teach HCPs,** so obesity pharmacotherapy started in routine practice is more often continued — and when treatment stops, patients and clinicians have a credible plan?
**Decision owners (company):** Medical Affairs with Clinical Development, Medical Education and Access
**Why external advisors:** trial persistence ≠ routine persistence; education-versus-study trade-offs need challenge
slides.takeaway: Success = advice that could surprise us — including disagreement.

left.heading: Simulated findings in SYN field notes and safety cases
bullets: Acute pancreatitis hospitalisation during titration (OBS-003)
Pregnancy exposures (OBS-009; CASE-03; MI-004)
Injector failure / incomplete dose — PQC (CASE-02)
Off-label HFpEF use with outcome (OBS-013)
Severe dehydration after vomiting; severe constipation with hospital assessment

right.heading: Handling rules
bullets: **Workshop:** do NOT send these to real pharmacovigilance systems
**Real programmes:** escalate per company SOP; the reporting clock starts at company awareness
Verbatim quotes stay in the AE surface file, not in this deck

slides.title: On-treatment efficacy is not the binding constraint
slides.design: Randomised, placebo-controlled · STEP 1 n=1,961 (no diabetes) · STEP 5 n=304
bullets: STEP 5 ETD −12.6 pp (95% CI −15.3 to −9.8) — on-treatment durability
**Limitation:** selected trial populations plus lifestyle co-intervention ≠ unselected primary care
slides.takeaway: Implication: sustaining benefit is a continuation, access and counselling problem.

slides.title: Withdrawal RCTs: continued therapy maintains weight loss
slides.design: Randomised withdrawal after open-label lead-in · STEP 4 (semaglutide) · SURMOUNT-4 (tirzepatide)
bullets: STEP 4 difference −14.8 pp (95% CI −16.0 to −13.5)
SURMOUNT-4: ≥80% of lead-in loss kept in 89.5% vs 16.6%
**Fair balance:** GI adverse events more common with continued active drug
**Gap:** taper / switch strategies not settled (NCT07832084 not yet recruiting)

slides.title: After cessation, regain is large and patterned
slides.design: Meta-regression of RCTs after GLP-1RA cessation · SURMOUNT-4 post-hoc (associative)

items.label: of lost weight regained at 1 year
SYN: ADIPOSYN regain at 1 year
items.note: Fictional workshop profile — not real data

bullets: SURMOUNT-4 post-hoc: greater regain associated with greater reversal of waist, BP, lipids and HbA1c (PMID 41284285; associative)
slides.takeaway: Education implication: an unplanned stop is a foreseeable clinical event — counsel accordingly.

slides.title: Routine practice: the persistence gap
slides.design: Observational · US commercial claims, Wegovy pens · n=15,811
bullets: Narrative review: real-world persistence often suboptimal in year 1 — GI AEs, cost, perceived efficacy, fear of rare AEs (PMID 42168641)
SYN field (OBS-019): clinicians report trial discontinuation understates practice
**Limitation:** claims incompletely capture reasons for stopping; geography-specific

slides.title: Cardiometabolic stakes — class evidence is agent-specific
slides.design: SELECT · randomised, placebo-controlled · adults ≥45 y, BMI ≥27, established CVD, no diabetes · n=17,604
bullets: **Board question:** what may HCPs be taught from class data, and what requires product-specific evidence?
slides.takeaway: Do NOT transfer SELECT to fictional ADIPOSYN — the SYN landscape states no product CVOT.
